composition.title: Battery Storage
composition.body: Batteries provide a practical method to store that electricity for use at night or during cloudy days.

brief.goal: Help teachers explain the relationship between solar generation and batteries
keyPoints: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity
Batteries store energy for later use
Understanding the flow of solar power
openQuestions: What specific misconceptions about solar and batteries should we avoid?

flow.title: The Solar-Energy Flow: Generation Meets Storage
flow.summary: This three-beat flow explains the core concept for teachers: solar panels generate electricity from sunlight, while batteries act as storage to power devices later. The narrative moves simply from source to capture to retention.

beats.title: Solar Generation
beats.audienceText: Sunlight is pure energy that can be captured by solar panels.
beats.speakerNotes: Begin with the concept of sunlight as a raw resource, then introduce solar panels as the mechanism that converts this light into usable electricity.
beats.visualDirection: An animation showing sunlight rays hitting photovoltaic cells and transforming into flowing electrons.

beats.title: Energy Capture
beats.audienceText: Once energy is captured as electricity, it requires a way to move power from where it is made to where it is needed.
beats.speakerNotes: Explain that the electricity generated at a specific moment may not be needed there immediately. Introduce the need to transport that electricity to different locations.
beats.visualDirection: A stylized road or pathway leading away from a solar panel array, representing the movement of electricity.

beats.title: Battery Storage
beats.audienceText: Batteries provide a practical method to store that electricity for use at night or during cloudy days.
beats.speakerNotes: Conclude by connecting the concept of stored energy to batteries. Explain how they act as 'containers' that keep the electrical power safe until it can be used later.
beats.visualDirection: A simple, clear graphic of a battery being filled with an electric symbol and then releasing it to light up a nearby device.

openQuestions: Are there specific visual metaphors teachers prefer for describing electricity flow and battery storage concepts without getting into technical details?
